findings.explanation: The study entry point identifies code, manuscript and data, and the three immediate component paths sit below the enclosing root. The nested source URL defect concerns reachability; it does not remove this structural common root.

Following root/data/raw_eyegaze exposes a nested acquisition-source gitlink with an absolute host-local URL. Other consumed datasets have project-relative boundaries. Partial captures this concrete recursive defect without claiming a failed download.

The main computation installs the linked classifier and declares numerical and rendering packages. Package declarations satisfy the native inclusion interpretation; dependency completeness and upstream environment gaps are distinct questions under must/010 and must/015.
The frozen tree and native history contain versioned numerical definitions, source and environment changes. A coordinator source-only capture is not evidence of untracked author changes.

The inventory supplies annex keys for image layers, including the 1,750,877,184-byte layer, and the data documentation describes annex retrieval. Payload absence in the inspection package does not invalidate the observed large-content tracking mechanism.

The root run declares container/image as an extra input and names the generated outputs. The linked label run instead records ambient Python through compute_all.sh without an exact environment. The root analysis consumes these labels, making partial appropriate across the declared boundary.

The root installation instructions are usable in form, but the included label component has an unqualified Reproduce README naming code/preprocess_eyegaze_recordings.submit, code/detect_events.submit and Python implementation files absent from its complete frozen inventory. Its actual recorded computation uses compute_all.sh. Because linked computational components are in scope, the root-only met overlooks a concrete documented-route/mechanism disagreement under native rule 10.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the declared recursive scope and identify the stale label instructions; retain credit for the clear root README. This finding is separate from the root README explicitly labeling its own older route.

findings.explanation: The root results and manuscript have named starting commands backed by a recorded analysis command and a registered target. The disclosed historical result difference does not itself make that starting point unclear. Upstream label documentation remains a separate deficiency noted under must/007.

The root analysis constructs relative paths, while linked scheduler generators hardcode an author working directory and Python executable. Those are actual host paths; paths used solely inside the image build are not equivalent violations.

The main script imports map to the container packages and local classifier; DataLad has an explicit optional fallback after host-side provisioning. The linked documented Condor route assumes Condor and Python 2.7 without its own complete environment specification. Partial has direct support, although the stale missing script problem should also be stated.

The supplied adapter requires a usable docker executable and non-root invocation, and the linked scheduler setup inherits host state and an author directory. The documented platform/version list does not explain those configuration assumptions, so partial is justified.

There is a clear list of host prerequisites and numerical/manuscript packages. This checklist item asks whether requirements are documented as a list; it need not duplicate the separate dependency-completeness and undocumented-assumption failures.

The environment recipe, execution registration and archive metadata are versioned beside code and data links. This pass establishes version control for the supplied specifications, not that an absent upstream specification exists.

The native history provides an executable build/save command, an actual recipe adjustment and a later recorded image conversion. These are concrete tracked maintenance actions rather than a lockfile introduction alone. Matching should/008 and duplicate flags are appropriate.

The root archive identifies an exact image, and the adapter executes its computed configuration hash rather than a floating tag. However, the in-scope label-generating computation uses an unspecified host Python environment. The assessment recognizes that same gap under must/006, so an object-wide met here overstates which environments a recipient can attempt to replicate exactly.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the stated scope: exact root analysis image supplied, exact label-generation environment absent. Preserve the distinction between a pinned archive and a reproducible Dockerfile rebuild.

findings.explanation: The frozen annex location logs are availability claims, not recipient retrieval receipts. The inspection restriction prevents verifying exact content access. Not-checked correctly preserves that uncertainty without treating absent captured bytes as an observed access failure.

The declared root environment is obtained through clone/rerun and used through the named docker-make registration. Both mechanism and instructions exist. This supports the documented environment-use procedure, while the unavailable exact upstream environment is handled separately.

Root and linked repositories use Git with DataLad/git-annex for large data. The shared Git-based model is visible in the component links and source histories rather than inferred solely from a DataLad name.

Classifier CI is a test definition for one component, and a historical completed analysis does not establish recurring full-workflow testing. Keeping the recurrence question not-checked is better supported than either a pass or an absence claim.

Raw inputs, derived event labels and classifier code have separate pinned repository boundaries; the root separates analysis, image specification and figures by path. This is useful functional modularity without requiring every directory to be a submodule.

The exit-zero historical analysis used the Docker adapter, whose run operation creates a new container. Native rules expressly accept equivalent completed-run evidence, so a fresh execution by this reviewer is unnecessary for this historical test claim. It does not prove the current archive can still be retrieved or the manuscript has been retested.

The root execution creates and removes a Docker container, but the explicitly included label pipeline directly invokes Python in the caller environment and does not spawn an isolated disposable environment. The scope used to identify its provenance and dependency defects must also apply to this all-executions property.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial: the root analysis/manuscript route is disposable, while label generation reuses host state. If assessing only root execution instead, explicitly narrow the scope consistently across related criteria.

findings.explanation: One image build and one format conversion show historical maintenance, not repeated tests that the exact result-generating environments can be reconstituted. The classifier CI installs dependencies independently. Not-checked accurately avoids inferring regularity from these isolated records.

The image is represented by content-addressed archived configuration and layers, with native creation/conversion records. This is stronger than merely naming a registry tag; missing inspection payloads do not prove the archive is absent from the research object.

The same executable maintenance process and tracked updates support this duplicate of must/014. Both native answers are met and both carry upstream-duplicate, avoiding a contradictory duplicate judgment.

The supplied access declaration says no authentication or registration is required, and no restricted component is identified on the inspected study route. A host-local source URL demonstrates a portability problem, not access restriction. The empty-subject N/A is defensible within this inspection boundary.

Independently maintained datasets and classifier code have explicit submodule boundaries. Following those links reveals the host-local acquisition-source URL, so partial is warranted without reclassifying ordinary Python packages as project modules.

The machine-readable module map and root reproduction narrative provide some structure, but no integrated account explains the different classifier revisions or how to recombine them. The label README describes a different obsolete mechanism, which further limits the documentation.

Raw inputs, event-table outputs and the classifier have separate version identities and explicit file interfaces. The enclosing pins retain known combinations while a component evolves. This supports independent update boundaries; it should not be read as a promise that arbitrary incompatible versions work together.

Submodule pins compose source and data, while the registration and recorded input/output selections compose execution. These are concrete composition mechanisms even though some component documentation and access paths need repair.

DataLad commands and nested module declarations give navigable paths and source URLs. The disjunctive documentation-or-tooling item can pass on this tooling despite the incomplete explanatory map under may/002.

limitations: Inspection only: no network requests, payload acquisition, scientific workflow execution, container build or replay. Missing annex/container/scientific payloads are capture omissions, not observed retrieval failures.

Used only the assigned anonymized JSON, pinned native instrument, and the frozen corpus reached through root documentation/module links. No peer reviews, results directory or other assessments were consulted.

Manifest SHA256 e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499 was verified; 267 captured source/history files matched their hashes. Content hashes verify capture identity, not scientific correctness.

The native checklist pin check and response validator passed. All 31 IDs were checked semantically; missing value fields are allowed because the native encoder derives them. The supplied JSON has no aggregate score or report denominator to audit; its status counts cover 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY, with unknown and N/A distinct.

Original raw probe receipts and the separate assessment report were outside the assigned input boundary. Assertions about probe overrides were checked against source where possible, but exact original probe output and report arithmetic were not independently audited.

The external Docker adapter is supplied through a release-tag URL rather than a commit URL; review citations bind it to its frozen SHA256 locator. Historical exit-zero records are repository evidence, not execution observed by this reviewer.

Native met requires support across the declared object. The requested revisions apply that boundary to linked label generation consistently with the assessment own provenance and dependency findings. Root-only execution remains stronger than the recursive computation boundary.
No verified observed runtime model identity was available; model_observed remains null. Agreement in this independent review is not human approval.
